What `github.blockers` quotes every name and piece of text read from GitHub before it goes into the Markdown `answer`, which the PR-blockers Action also writes to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. A fork's workflow names its own check runs, and any integration with status access sets a status's context, description and target URL. Before this PR that text was rendered as live Markdown: headings, links, images, and instructions to a model. - `BlockerAnalysis.Quote` renders each untrusted string as one inline code span, capped at 100 characters. It strips control and format characters and turns a backtick into `'`. It applies to check names, status context and description, reviewer login, base ref, tag, and required-check names. - `BlockerAnalysis.Link` keeps an evidence URL only if it is an absolute http(s) URL, and encodes parentheses and spaces. - The Bricks.GitHub README and the `answer` output description now say this. Found by the MCP host adversarial audit (finding M3). ## Rebased onto #874 (043a37a5a) - The only conflict was the `BlockerAnalysis` class doc comment. I kept #874's text and added the untrusted-text paragraph after it. #874's new messages are all fixed wording, so none of them needed quoting. - The brick version stays at **1.1.0**. #874 bumped it, it is unreleased, and both changes ship in 0.4.0. - #874's new test expectations now use backticked check names (`` `build (ubuntu-latest)` ``, `` `coverage` ``, `` `lint` ``). - The CHANGELOG has a bullet under #874's 1.1.0 entry. ## Verified - `GitHubBlockersBrickTests`: 51/51 in the devtest container (`scripts/test-in-container.sh`). - Mutation checks, run before the rebase: KILLED 3/46, 4/46, 2/46 (Quote not applied to check names, control characters kept, Link accepting non-http schemes).
